posts.body:
Hi all,

Am wondering if I can delve into the experience of all the moms on the forum for a recommendation of a lightweight reversible pushchair? So far, I have only come across the Graco Evo, which though ticks the right boxes am looking for alternatives to compare. So anyone else who has a lightweight reversible pushchair they would recommend?

posts.body:
Quinny Zapp Xtra, parent faces, forward faces and will take a car seat.

Petite Star Njoy Bubbble, parent faces and forward faces.

Bugaboo bee, parent faces, forward faces and will take a car seat too.

M&P Urbo, parent faces, forward faces, will take a car seat and optional carry cot.

All lightweight. Hth x

posts.body: we liked the Evo but it doesnt have isofix so discounted it. We've gone for the M & P zoom
posts.body_with_quotes: we liked the Evo but it doesnt have isofix so discounted it. We've gone for the M & P zoom

posts.body: I have the Bugaboo Bee and love it. Miles better than any other pushchair I have ever had with other children, and as light as a McLaren. Result!
posts.body_with_quotes: I have the Bugaboo Bee and love it. Miles better than any other pushchair I have ever had with other children, and as light as a McLaren. Result!

posts.body: I was going to say the Quinny Zapp, my friend has it. All my buggies have been rear facing but not lightweight! x
posts.body_with_quotes: I was going to say the Quinny Zapp, my friend has it. All my buggies have been rear facing but not lightweight! x

posts.body:
Thanks for all the suggestions!

We are now liking the look of the M&P Urbo, though the Quinny Zapp comes close but we prefer the horizontal handlebars. I can't at the moment justify the cost of the Bugaboo Bee, but I guess its to some peoples preference.

posts.body:
iCandy Cherry is a very lightweight frame with parent-facing - but IS a 2 part fold.

Might be worth looking second hand if you're wanting a bit more buggy for your money as well though (just be careful cos I've heard of some issues with fake bugaboos).
